chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Nāsibī (one who harbors enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) whose enmity and hostility are known. Can the believer marry him, while he is capable of repelling him (from the marriage), and he does not know of the repulsion? He said: 'The believer does not marry the Nāsibīyah (female Nāsibī), nor does the Nāsibī marry a believing woman, nor does the weak (or humble) man marry a believing woman.'

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: Nāsibī, one who harbors enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for marriage between a believer and a Nāsibī according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the marital eligibility of the *Nāsibī* (one known for enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt), establishing a prohibition on intermarriage with believers to preserve religious integrity. It further extends this restriction to the *Mustaḍʿaf* (often interpreted as a man of lower social standing or specific status) marrying a believing woman, highlighting the importance of compatibility in faith and status. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that marital unions should not compromise the spiritual standing of the believer.
